uyyama: [Yādicchakanāma]  CL=7 A person named uyyama (who is a bodhisatta , a prince Siddhattha). See -Uyyamavhaya.
uyyodhika:
[U+yudha+ṇvu]  CL=9 1. A place where fighting/combat takes place by repeatedly advancing and striking - battlefield
2. The act of advancing and striking in combat/warfare
3. Uyyodhika Sikkhapadha - A training rule related to military activities
uyyoga:
[U+yuja+ṇa]  CL=8 1. Making effort/exertion (uyyoga)
2. Time or place of advancing with effort/military expedition
(Related to uyyogakala - time of expedition/campaign)
3. Deterioration, decline, destruction
(Related to uyyogamukha - facing decline/destruction)
uyyogakāla: [Uyyoga+kāla]  CL=7 While marching to battle, one should strive more.
uyyojaka: [U+yuja+ṇvu]  CL=7 [In thī-uyyojikā.]  A person who urges another one to do something.
uyyojana:
[U+yuja+yu]  CL=7 1. Uyyojana - The act of urging, encouraging, or instructing
2. Words of encouragement, instruction, or urging
3. Day/time of giving instruction or encouragement
uyyojanadivasa: [Uyyojana+divasa]  CL=7 A day when someone urges someone to do something.
uyyojanattha: [Uyyojana+attha]  CL=7 The meaning of urging or commanding.
uyyojanika:
[Uyyojana+ika]  CL=8 1. Having the quality of urging/encouraging
2. One who is capable of urging/encouraging
See: uyyojanika-patisaṃyutta
uyyojanikapaṭisaṃyutta: [Uyyojanika]  CL=7 [Paṭisaṃyutta] That which is associated with urging or commanding speech.
uyyojemi: [U+yuja+ṇe+mi]  CL=7 A person who urges another person to do something. See-Uyyojeti
uyyojenta: [U+yuja+ṇe+anta]  CL=7 [In thī uyyojentī]  A person who urges or a person who orders another person to do something.
uyyojessasi: [U+yuja+ṇe+ssasi]  CL=7 He will urges another person to do something. See-Uyyojeti.
uyyojessatha: [U+yuja+ṇe+ssatha]  CL=7 He will urges another person to do something. See-Uyyojeti.
uyyojessati: [U+yuja+ṇe+ssati]  CL=7 He will urges another person to do something. See-Uyyojeti.
uyyojesuṃ: [U+yuja+ṇe+uuṃ]  CL=7 They urged another person to do something. See-Uyyojeti.
uyyojetabba: [U+yuja+ṇe+tabba]  CL=7 A person who urges another person to do something.
uyyojetha: [U+yuja+ṇe+tha]  CL=7 They order or command and sent. See-Uyyojeti.
uyyojeti: [U+yuja+ṇe+ti]  CL=7 He urges, sends, and causes to connect.
uyyojetu: [U+yuja+ṇe+tu]  CL=7 May you urge and send. See-Uyyojeti.
uyyojeyya: [U+yuja+ṇe+ṇe+eyya]  CL=7 He should urge and send. See-Uyyojeti.
uyyojita: [U+yuja+ta]  CL=7 A person who should be urgerd and sent.
uyyojitacitta: [Uyyojita+citta]  CL=7 A person who possesses a motivated mind.
uyyojiyamāna: [U+yuja+ya+māna]  CL=7 A person who should be urgerd and sent.
uyyojīyamāna: [U+yuja+ya+māna]  CL=7 A person who is sent
uyyutta:
[U+yuja+ta]  CL=8 1. One who departs (from town/village); assembled troops departing (from town/village); marching army
2. One who makes effort/strives
3. That which should be engaged with/undertaken
See: uyyutta-sikkhāpada
uyyuttacaturaṅgasenādassana: [Uyyuttacaturaṅgasenā+dassana]  CL=7 Watching the army completed with four elements which goes to the battle field.
uyyuttapayutta: [Uyyutta+payutta]  CL=7 A person who puts in effort continuously.
uyyuttasenā:
[Uyyuttā+senā]  CL=8 1. Training rule concerning marching army (uyyutta-senā-sikkhāpada)
2. Marching army, advancing troops (adj.)
3. Having/containing marching army
See: uyyutta-senā-sikkhāpada
uyyuttāvudha:
[Uyyutta+āvudha]  CL=8 One who is equipped with/bearing weapons, armed person
- In literal sense (mukhya): refers to soldiers/warriors
- In figurative sense (upacāra): refers to elephants ridden by soldiers
uyyutāvudha: Uyuta Wuda Uyuta (Ta) Wuda - Look. တိပိ၊⁇ ခ, 602 uyyutāvudha Uyutavudha (ti) [Uyutta + Avudha] Armed He
uyyāhi: [U+yā+a+hi]  CL=7 May he goes away. See-Uyyāti.
uyyāna:
[U+yā+yu]  CL=7 (1) A park. (2) Going.
[Nīti,dhā.138. Ullokentā yanti janā etasminti uyyānaṃ. Dhāna,ṭī. 538.]
uyyānadvāra: [Uyyāna+dvāra]  CL=7 The gate of the garden.
uyyānagamanasīla: [Uyyānagamana+sīla]  CL=7 One who is used to going to the garden.
uyyānagata: [Uyyāna+gata]  CL=7 A simile of searching the garden.
uyyānagavesakaopamma: [Uyyānagavesaka+opumma]  CL=7 A simile of searching the garden.
uyyānakāla: [Uyyāna+kāla]  CL=7 A period when someone is engaged in playing within the garden.
uyyānakīḷakā: [Uyyāna+kīḷi(ḷa)kā]  CL=7 A time of one who is hunting in the garden as fun.
uyyānakīḷamaṇḍala: [Uyyānakīḷā+maṇḍala]  CL=7 The area of the garden.
uyyānakīḷāmaṇḍala: [Uyyānakīḷā+maṇḍala]  CL=7 Roundabout or circle thing in play area
uyyānamakkaṭī: [Uyyāna+makkaṭī]  CL=10 The monkey stays in the garden.
uyyānaovaraka: [Uyyāna+ovaraka]  CL=10 A chamber/room built in a garden.
uyyānapokkharaṇī: [Uyyāna+pokkharaṇī] (thī) CL=7 A rectangular shape pond that dugs in the garden.
uyyānapākāramatthaka: [Uyyānapākāra+matthaka] (pu,na) CL=7 Top of the garden wall.
uyyānapāla: [Uyyāna+pāla] (ti) CL=7 One who is a parkkeeper. A gardener.
uyyānapālaputta: [Uyyānapāla+putta] (ti) CL=7 Son of a gardener or parkkeeper.
uyyānarakkhaka: [Uyyāna+rakkhaka] (ti) CL=7 One who is a parkkeeper.
uyyānarasa: [Uyyāna+rasa] (pu) CL=7 Taking pleasure in the garden. One who is taking pleasure in living in the garden.
uyyānasampanna: [Uyyāna+sampanna] (ti) CL=7 Walking around in the garden.
uyyānaseṭṭha: [Uyyāna+seṭṭha] (na) CL=7 A beautiful park or noble garden.
uyyānavanacārikā: [Uyyānavana+cārikā] (thī) CL=7 Walking around in the garden.
uyyānavanakīḷā: [Uyyānavana+kīḷā]  CL=8 Hunting for sport in the garden.
uyyānavanamālī: [Uyyānavanamālā+ī] (ti) CL=7 [In Thī uyyānavanamālinī.] The flowers in the garden.
uyyānavicaraṇa: [Uyyāna+vicaraṇa] (na) CL=7 Walking around in the garden.
uyyāpenti: [U+yā+ṇāpe+anti] (kā,kri) CL=7 They cause to go up (realm). See - Uyyāpeti.
uyyāpeti: [U+yā+ṇāpe+ti] (kā,kri) CL=7 He causes to go up (realm).
uyyāta: [U+yā+ta] (ti) CL=7 One who is going out.
uyyāti:
[U+yā+a+ti]  CL=10 Etymology: [u + yā + a + ti]
Meaning:
1. To go
2. To depart
3. To move or travel in an unconventional way/not as a regular journey
uyyojanikapaṭisayutta: [Uyyojanika]  CL=7 [Paṭisaṃyutta] That which is associated with urging or commanding speech.
uyyojesu: [U+yuja+ṇe+uuṃ]  CL=7 They urged another person to do something. See-Uyyojeti.
